title: European Ash: Ancient Ash Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: Ash dieback is working west across Europe, which changes how you look at an old one. Four ashes mapped, including a 37 metre trunk in Prague.
intro: Ash is the tree Europe is losing right now. A fungus from east Asia, harmless to the ashes it evolved alongside, arrived in Poland and has since worked its way west across the continent, which puts a different weight on the four mapped here. The tallest is in Prague, a 37 metre trunk in the one corner of Strahov Monastery the monks left open to the public, protected since 2007 and among the most massive ashes recorded in the Czech Republic. Gdansk's is older than the rifle factory built around it, roughly 280 years against the works that once turned out 2,500 guns a day. Edinburgh's stands in a park whose house is a roofless shell. Munich's carries no age, no size and no history in the city ordinance, only three words: extremely wide-spreading crown.
